It can be incredibly frustrating to feel like you have no control around food, especially when it seems like others can easily stop. Please know you are definitely not alone in this. Sweets and desserts are often designed to be highly pleasurable, which makes it very natural for our brains to want to keep eating them long past the point of physical fullness. 

Instead of being hard on yourself, it might help to approach this with gentle curiosity. Sometimes, restricting certain foods can actually make the cravings stronger, or eating might be serving as a way to cope with stress or other emotions. You might find it helpful to explore mindful eating practices, which focus on savoring food and tuning into your body's signals without judgment. Speaking with a registered dietitian or a therapist who specializes in our relationship with food could also provide you with personalized, compassionate strategies to help you feel more at peace with eating.
